title: fix: preserve visitor revocation through provider failures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

An explicit Visitor Access revoke can leave a grant active when the Cloudflare update fails. The durable record keeps its original expiry, so cleanup waits until that date; a permanent grant never becomes eligible for the normal expiry sweep.

The plugin now records immediate expiry before contacting Cloudflare. This preserves the requested removal for the existing recovery sweep even when the provider fails or its response is lost.

## User Impact

After a failed revoke, the startup or hourly sweep can retry removing the policy entry. The revoke still reports the provider error, and the record remains available for reconciliation until cleanup succeeds. Successful cleanup deletes the record, and an intentional later invitation can renew access.

This repair covers durable retry of provider-policy cleanup. Existing-login invalidation and cancellation of running work are outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin's serialized grant service already owns the durable record and policy read/modify/write sequence. Updating its existing expiry field before provider I/O keeps removal recoverable within that owner. The provider operation must still settle successfully before cleanup removes the record. The README now documents this ordering and retry behavior.

## Evidence

The existing visitor-service failure test covers active, permanent, and already-expired grants. With the regression assertions on the unchanged production baseline, the active and permanent revoke cases failed and the other 20 cases passed. With the correction, all 22 cases passed on the same Blacksmith Testbox using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/visitor-access/src/visitors.test.ts`. Provider responses were simulated; no live policy or deployment was changed. [Regression run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35526009769).

Changed-file formatting, targeted lint, line-cap and assertion-safety checks, and diff hygiene passed. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35526472654) passed, including production and test types, affected extension checks, docs, and source boundaries. Independent source review found no blocker, and [ClawSweeper's exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153878#issuecomment-5751504701) returned Platinum with no findings.
